item.title: Editor Rose Friedman, who helped shape NPR's cultural coverage, dies at 38
item.description: Friedman was in her early 20s when she landed her first position as an editorial assistant at NPR. She became an editor and reporter, and a co-creator of the annual Books We Love reading guide.

item.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
item.description: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

item.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
item.description: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

item.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
item.description: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

item.title: Syrian regime planned American journalist's kidnapping for weeks
item.description: New reporting finds the abduction of journalist Austin Tice was planned by the Syrian government for weeks.

item.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
item.description: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

item.title: There's 'Hope' for this divisive alien invasion film that mixes art and schlock
item.description: Shape-shifting aliens attack a South Korean border town in Hope, a big-budget thriller that blends third-rate CGI with exhilarating action scenes.

item.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
item.description: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

item.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
item.description: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

item.title: South Africa 'feels like a prison' for women amid spate of femicides
item.description: South Africa has some of the highest rates of violence against women in the world, and a spate of killings of nine women in the same area in recent weeks has led to renewed outrage.
